mekki-muskil:107-107.t:
His saying {الأوليان}: whoever reads it in the nominative (marfūʿ) and in the dual makes it a badal (substitute) for آخرَانِ, or for the latent pronoun in يقومان. It has also been said that it is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil; lit. "the object whose agent is not named") of اسْتَحَقَّ, on the reading of those who put a ḍamma on the tāʾ (اسْتُحِقَّ), on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "of those against whom the sin of the two first (الْأَوليين) became due"; and عَلَيْهِم would then have the sense of فيهم ("among them"). Whoever reads الْأَوَّلين, as the plural of أول ("first"), places it in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a badal from الَّذين, or from the hāʾ and mīm in عَلَيْهِم.
His saying {لَشَهَادَتنَا}: the lām is the answer to the oath in His saying فيقسمان ("and they both swear").

mekki-muskil:108-108.t: His saying {أَن يَأْتُوا}: it is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) by omission of the preposition, its implied form being بِأَن يَأْتُوا; and similar to it is أَن آمنُوا. Abū Muḥammad Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: This verse is among the most difficult things in the Qur'an in its i'rab, its meaning, its exegesis and its legal rulings, and I have devoted a separate book to it in which I explained it.

mekki-muskil:110-110.t:
His saying {إِن هَذَا إِلَّا سحر}: إِن has the sense of مَا ("not"), and هَذَا points to what ʿĪsā (Jesus), peace be upon him, brought. It is also possible that هَذَا points to the Prophet, peace be upon him, on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "this is nothing but one possessed of sorcery (ذُو سحر)". As for whoever reads سَاحر ("a sorcerer") with an alif, هَذَا points to the Prophet, peace be upon him, with no omission. And it may possibly point to the Gospel (al-Injīl), in which case the active participle stands in the position of a maṣdar (verbal noun), just as they said عائذا بِاللَّه من شَرها ("seeking refuge in Allah from its evil"), meaning عياذا بِاللَّه ("refuge in Allah").
His saying {فتنفخ فِيهَا}: the hāʾ refers back to the shape (الْهَيْئَة), and "shape" is a maṣdar standing in the position of "the thing shaped" (المهيأ), because blowing does not take place into the shape; it only takes place into the thing shaped. It may also refer back to the birds (الطير), because it is feminine. And whoever reads طائرا ("a bird"), it is permissible that طَائِر be a plural, like الحامل, so the pronoun in فِيهَا is made feminine because it refers back to the group.

mekki-muskil:116-116.t: His saying {أَنْت علام الغيوب} and وَأَنت الْعَزِيز: أَنْت is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf, or a mubtadaʾ (subject), or a separating pronoun (fāṣila) with no grammatical position.

mekki-muskil:117-117.t:
His saying {أَن اعبدوا الله}: أَن is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position, in the sense of أَي ("that is"). It may also be in the position of the accusative as a badal from مَا.
His saying {مَا دمت فيهم}: مَا is in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), and what governs it is شَهِيد.

mekki-muskil:119-119.t:
His saying {هَذَا يَوْم ينفع}: whoever puts يَوْم in the nominative makes it the khabar (predicate) of هَذَا, and هَذَا points to the Day of Resurrection, and the clause is in the position of the accusative by the verb "to say" (al-qawl). As for whoever puts يَوْم in the accusative, he makes it an adverbial (ẓarf) of the saying, and هَذَا points to the narratives and the account that preceded; that is: Allah says these words on a day on which [truthfulness] benefits. So هَذَا points to the narratives that preceded, namely His saying وَإِذ قَالَ الله يَا عِيسَى up to His saying من دون الله. Allah thus reported what had not yet happened using the past tense, because of the certainty of its coming to be and occurring. And it is permissible for يَوْم to be a predicate of هَذَا because it points to an event, and adverbs of time can be predicates of events. According to the view of the Kufans, it is also possible that يَوْم ينفع is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its annexation to the verb; if that is so, its position may be accusative or nominative according to the explanation already given. But according to the Basrans, indeclinability occurs in an adverb (ẓarf) annexed to a verb only when the verb is indeclinable; when it is declinable, the adverb annexed to it is not made indeclinable, in their view.
His saying {خَالِدين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in لَهُم; أبدا is an adverb of time. The yāʾ in رَضِي replaces a wāw because of the kasra before it, since it is from الرضْوَان. The original form of رَضوا is رضووا: the vowel of the first wāw was transferred to the ḍād, and it was dropped because it was vowelless and the wāw after it, which is the plural pronoun, was also vowelless.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, exalted is He, {إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُم}: ما is in the position of the accusative as an exception from بَهِيمَة.
His saying {غير محلي الصَّيْد}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in أَوْفوا; it has also been said: from the kāf and mīm in لكم.
His saying {وَأَنْتُم حرم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in محلين. The nūn of محلين fell away because of its being put in genitive construct with الصَّيْد.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying {يَبْتَغُونَ}: in the position of the accusative, [relating] to آمين.
His saying {أَن صدوكم}: whoever reads إن with kasra, its meaning is: "if obstruction of you occurs, let not the hatred of those who obstruct you lead you to transgress"; so the obstruction is something awaited. What shows this is that in the reading (ḥarf) of Ibn Masʿūd it is إِن يصدوكم. So the meaning is: "if an obstruction occurs like the one done to you at first, then do not transgress." Like it, according to Sībawayh, is the poet's saying:
... أتغضب إِن أذنا قُتَيْبَة حزتا ...
(Will you be angry if the two ears of Qutayba are cut off?)
And that is something that had already happened; its meaning is only: "if the like of that happens, will you be angry?" The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is what precedes it. Whoever reads it with fatḥa (أَن), أن is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the exegesis (tafsīr) came accordingly, because the obstruction had already happened before the revelation of the verse: the verse was revealed in the year of the Conquest, the year eight, and the polytheists obstructed the Muslims from the Sacred House in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya, the year six. So the fatḥa is its proper case, and the exegesis and the history point to it, because the kasra indicates something that has not happened, and the fatḥa indicates something that has happened, been and passed. The parallel of that: if a man said to his wife, when she had already entered his house, "you are divorced if (إِن) you enter the house," with kasra on إن, she would not be divorced from him by her first entry, because it is a thing awaited; and if he said it with fatḥa (أَن, "because"), she would be divorced from him, because it is a thing that has been. The fatḥa of أن is only his knowledge of what has been and happened, and its kasra only indicates a thing awaited, which may or may not be. Both readings are good, each according to its meaning.
His saying {أَن تَعْتَدوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by يجرمنكم «[Translator's note: the source writes it «بيجر مِنْكُم».]». شنآن is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it is the fāʿil (agent) of يجرمنكم. The prohibition falls in wording on the hatred, but those addressed are meant by it, as you say لَا أرينك هَاهُنَا ("let me not see you here"): the prohibition in wording is of the speaker, but what is meant by it is the one addressed. Like it is فَلَا تموتن إِلَّا وَأَنْتُم مُسلمُونَ, and like it is لَا يجرمنكم شقاقي. Whoever reads الشنآن with sukūn makes it a noun.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {فَمن اضْطر}: من is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and it is conditional; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فان الله غَفُور رَحِيم, and it is the khabar (predicate). With it there is an omitted implied element, its implied form being "then indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful to him" (فان الله لَهُ غَفُور رَحِيم).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying {مَاذَا أحل لَهُم}: ما and ذا are one noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and أحل لَهُم is the khabar (predicate). Or, if you wish, you make ذا in the sense of الَّذِي, so that it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ and أحل لَهُم is its ṣila (relative clause). يَسْأَلُونَك does not govern ما in either view, because it is interrogative, and what precedes an interrogative does not govern it.
His saying {مكلبين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the tāʾ and mīm in علمْتُم.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying {محصنين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative pronoun in آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ; and like it is غير مسافحين, and like it is وَلَا متخذي أخدان, which is conjoined to غير مسافحين. You do not conjoin it to محصنين, because لا enters with it as an emphasis of the preceding negation, and there is no negation with محصنين. Or, if you wish, you make غير مسافحين and وَلَا متخذي a naʿt (adjective) of محصنين or a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in محصنين.
His saying {وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَة من الخاسرين}: what governs the adverbial is omitted, its implied form being "and he is a loser in the Hereafter" (وَهُوَ خاسر فِي الْآخِرَة); His saying من الخاسرين points to the omission. If you take the alif and lām in الخاسرين as not being in the sense of الَّذِي, it is permitted for الخاسرين to govern the adverbial.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying {وأرجلكم}: whoever reads it in the accusative conjoins it to الْأَيْدِي and الْوُجُوه. Whoever reads it in the genitive conjoins it to الرؤوس and implies what requires washing, so the verse is unabrogated (muḥkama), as though He said "and your feet with washing" (وأرجلكم غسلا). Al-Akhfash and Abū ʿUbayda said: the genitive in it is by proximity (al-jiwār), and the meaning is washing; that is far-fetched, and the Quran is not to be construed according to it. A group said: it is conjoined to الرؤوس, and the verse is abrogated by the Sunna, which requires washing the feet; it is abrogated according to this reading. It has been said: it is conjoined to الرؤوس, its wording unabrogated, but the setting of a limit indicates washing; since He limited the washing of the feet to the ankles just as He limited the washing of the hands to the elbows, it is known that it is a washing like the hands. And it has been said: mash (wiping) in the language occurs in the sense of washing; one says تمسحت للصَّلَاة, i.e. "I performed ablution"; so the Sunna made clear that what is meant by the wiping of the feet, when it is read in the genitive, is washing.
His saying {فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدا}: whoever takes الصَّعِيد as the earth or the face of the earth makes صَعِيدا accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf). Whoever takes الصَّعِيد as dust makes it accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) from which the preposition has been omitted, i.e. بصعيد. طيبا is its naʿt (adjective), i.e. "clean." It has also been said that الطّيب means "lawful," so its accusative is as a maṣdar (verbal noun) or as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {شُهَدَاء}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in قوامين; it may also be a second khabar (predicate) of كان; and it has been said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of قوامين.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying {وعد الله الَّذين آمنُوا}: the basic rule of وعد is that it takes two objects, and it is permitted to confine it to one of them. So it occurred in this verse: it takes one object, namely الَّذين; then He explained the omitted object, namely the promise, by His saying لَهُم مغْفرَة وَأجر عَظِيم.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t:
His saying {فبمَا نقضهم}: like what is in [the sura of] al-Nisāʾ.
His saying {يحرفُونَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the owners of the hearts.
His saying {إِلَّا قَلِيلا مِنْهُم}: an exception from the hāʾ and mīm in مِنْهُم.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying {وَمن الَّذين قَالُوا إِنَّا نَصَارَى أَخذنَا ميثاقهم}: من is attached to أَخذنَا, i.e. "and We took from those who said 'We are Christians' their covenant," like your saying من زيد أخذت درهما ("from Zayd I took a dirham"). It is not permitted to intend الَّذين as postponed after الْمِيثَاق, because of the pronoun preceding the overt noun; rather, you intend it to be after أَخذنَا and before الْمِيثَاق, because both are objects of أَخذنَا, so neither has any priority over the other in coming first. The hāʾ and mīm refer to الَّذين, and the position of الَّذين is not to be after ميثاقهم; therefore it is permitted. Do you not see that if you said ضرب غُلَامه زيدا ("his servant struck Zayd") it would not be permitted, and it is not permitted to intend الغلام as postponed, because it is in its proper place and rank, since the right of the agent is to come before the object, so it is not intended to be in other than its position? If you made الغلام accusative and زيد nominative, it would be permitted, because you intend الغلام and the pronoun to be postponed, since postponement is its position, so you intend it in its position after the agent. The Kufans disallowed most of this, and they took the verse as involving omission; its implied form according to them is "and among those who said 'We are Christians' are those whose covenant We took" (وَمن الَّذين قَالُوا إِنَّا نَصَارَى من أَخذنَا ميثاقهم). So the hāʾ and mīm refer to the omitted من, which is implied before the pronoun. Omitting من was permitted according to them just as it was permitted in His saying وَمَا منا إِلَّا لَهُ مقَام, i.e. "except one who has," and as He said من الَّذين هادوا يحرفُونَ, i.e. "some who distort."

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying {يبين لكم}: يبين is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from رَسُولنَا; and like it is the second [occurrence], and like it is يعْفُو.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t:
His saying {يهدي بِهِ الله}: يهدي is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب; or, if you wish, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from كتاب, because you have qualified it with مبين, so it has come close to the definite, and the ḥāl from it has become good. And like it are ويخرجهم and ويهديهم.
His saying {سبل السَّلَام}: an object from which the preposition has been omitted, i.e. إِلَى سبل السَّلَام ("to the ways of peace").

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying {أَن تَقولُوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying {خاسرين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in تنقلبوا.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying {أنعم الله}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in يخَافُونَ; it may also be in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of رجلَيْنِ; and likewise His saying من الَّذين يخَافُونَ.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying {أبدا}: an adverb of time, and مَا داموا is a badal (substitute) for أبدا, and it is a badal of part for whole.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying {إِلَّا نَفسِي وَأخي}: أخي is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to نَفسِي. Or, if you wish, you conjoin it to the noun (ism) of أنّ, and its khabar (predicate) is omitted because the first points to it, as though He said "and my brother possesses only himself" (وان أخي لَا يملك إِلَّا نَفسه). Or, if you wish, you make الأخ in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), conjoined to the position of أنّ and what it governs, and you imply the khabar as in the first. Or, if you wish, you conjoin it to the latent pronoun in أملك, so it is in the position of the nominative.

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying {أَرْبَعِينَ سنة}: أَرْبَعِينَ is an adverb of time, and what governs it is يتيهون, on the basis that you take the prohibition as having no time-limit, as came in the exegesis that none of them entered it, only their sons entered it, and they all died in the wilderness. So on this view يتيهون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in عَلَيْهِم, and you do not pause at عَلَيْهِم on this view, unless you make يتيهون cut off from what precedes it, in which case you pause at عَلَيْهِم. If you give the prohibition a time-limit, namely forty years, you make أَرْبَعِينَ accusative by محرمة, and يتيهون is again a ḥāl from the hāʾ and mīm in عَلَيْهِم; on this view pausing at عَلَيْهِم is not permitted at all. You do not pause at أَرْبَعِينَ سنة at all on the first view, and you pause at it on this view if you make يتيهون cut off and not a ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:29-29.t: His saying {إِنِّي أُرِيد}: إِنِّي, إِنَّا, أَنا, لَكِنِّي, لَكنَّا and the like — all of it originally has three nūns, but one was dropped for lightness because three identical letters came together with no barrier between them; it has been used in much of the Quran in the original form, without omission. The view of al-Khalīl, according to what Sībawayh related from him, is that the omitted one is the one before the yāʾ, meaning the third. What reasoning requires, and what the people of knowledge hold, is that the one omitted from these nūns is the second, because if you dropped the third, the second would have to change to kasra in إِنِّي and لَكِنِّي, so omission and change would come together, and that is disliked; and if you dropped the first, the second would have to be assimilated into the third after removing its vowel and making it vowelless, and that is two omissions and a change; so dropping the second was more fitting. Moreover, from أنّ the second is sometimes dropped when they are [only] two nūns, so dropping that very one when they become three nūns is more fitting than dropping another. And if you dropped the third from أَنِّي, you would have to drop the third in أننا and لَكنَّا, and so drop the sign of the pronoun; that is not permitted, because it is a noun, and nouns are not dropped, nor is part of them dropped, because of identical letters coming together.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t: His saying {أَو فَسَاد فِي الأَرْض}: conjoined to نفس, i.e. "or without corruption." Al-Ḥasan read it in the accusative with the meaning "or he worked corruption" (أَو أفسد فَسَادًا), so it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying {أَن يقتلُوا}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of جَزَاء, because أَن with what follows it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); so it is a maṣdar predicated of a maṣdar, and it is identical to it. أو in His saying أَو يصلبوا, and the أو in what follows it, are for giving the imam a choice according to his own judgement (ijtihād); the scholars have several views on that. «[Translator's note: the source reads «وَهُوَ هُوَ وَاو فِي قَوْله», evidently for «وهو هو، وأو في قوله»; translated accordingly.]»

mekki-muskil:34-34.t: His saying {إِلَّا الَّذين تَابُوا}: accusative as an exception.

mekki-muskil:38-38.t:
His saying {وَالسَّارِق والسارقة}: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted according to Sībawayh; its implied form is "and among what is recited to you: the male thief and the female thief" (وَفِيمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُم السَّارِق والسارقة) or "among what has been prescribed for you." The preferred choice according to Sībawayh's school is the accusative in it, because it is a command, and a command is more fitting with the verb; and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it so. The preferred choice according to the Kufans is the nominative, as in the reading of the majority, because no particular thief is intended by it; so according to them it is like واللذان يأتيانها, by which two particular persons are not meant, and therefore the nominative was chosen. We have mentioned Sībawayh's reasoning in choosing the nominative in واللذان يأتيانها, and in His saying وَالسَّارِق والسارقة there is not the reason that is in واللذان.
His saying {جَزَاء بِمَا كسبا}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or, if you wish, a maṣdar (verbal noun); and like it is نكالا.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t:
His saying {وَمن الَّذين هادوا سماعون للكذب سماعون لقوم آخَرين لم يأتوك يحرفُونَ الْكَلم}: His saying سماعون and يحرفون are two adjectives of two omitted [nouns] that are nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes them is the khabar (predicate); its implied form is "a party who listen and a party who distort the words" (فريق سماعون وفريق يحرفُونَ الْكَلم). "In order to lie": He did not mean that they hear lies and accept them; He only meant that they listen in order to lie, and say what they did not hear; what shows this is His saying يحرفُونَ الْكَلم من بعد موَاضعه. It is also possible for يحرفُونَ to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in سماعون, and it would be the anticipated ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-muqaddara), i.e. "they listen, intending distortion," like His saying هَديا بَالغ الْكَعْبَة.
His saying {آخَرين} {لم يأتوك}: two adjectives of قوم.
His saying {يَقُولُونَ إِن أُوتِيتُمْ}: a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in يحرفُونَ. On this view one pauses at قُلُوبهم and begins with وَمن الَّذين هادوا, which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. It has also been said that سماعون is nominative on هم سماعون ("they are listeners"), a mubtadaʾ and khabar; so one pauses at هادوا on this view. The first view is better and more fitting. As for the second سماعون للكذب, it is nominative on an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are listeners to falsehood, devourers of the unlawful" (هم سماعون للكذب أكالون للسحت).

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying {النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذين أَسْلمُوا}: الَّذين is an adjective of النَّبِيُّونَ in the sense of praise and commendation, not in the sense of the adjective that comes to distinguish the one described from someone who does not have his attribute. Likewise you say رَأَيْت زيدا الْعَاقِل ("I saw Zayd the intelligent"): this adjective may be one you brought only for commendation and praise, like the verse, and it may be one you brought to distinguish Zayd the intelligent from another Zayd who is not intelligent. This [latter] is not permitted in the verse, because it is not possible that they had prophets who were not Muslims, as it is possible that there is another Zayd who is not intelligent. If you said رَأَيْت زيدا الْأَحْمَر ("I saw Zayd the red"), this is an adjective you brought to distinguish between Zayd the red and another Zayd, or other Zayds, who are not red — so know it — and this adjective admits no meaning other than this. If Zayd were known only by "the red," omitting الْأَحْمَر would not be permitted, because it would be part of the completion of his name.

mekki-muskil:45-45.t:
His saying {وَالْعين بِالْعينِ} and the nouns that follow it: whoever reads it in the accusative conjoins it to what أنّ governs, namely النَّفس, and بِالنَّفسِ is the khabar (predicate) of أنّ; likewise each genitive phrase is the khabar of what precedes it. Whoever reads الْعين, الْأنف and السّن in the nominative conjoins them according to the meaning, because the meaning of كتبنَا عَلَيْهِم is "We said to them: the life for the life," so it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). It has been said that it is a mubtadaʾ cut off from what precedes it. And it has been said that it is conjoined to the nominative pronoun latent in بِالنَّفسِ; even though it has not been emphasized, it is permitted, as He said مَا أشركنا وَلَا آبَاؤُنَا — and there is no proof in the addition of لا after the conjunction that it separated, because it comes after the conjunction. The genitive phrase is the khabar of each mubtadaʾ.
His saying {والجروح قصاص}: whoever reads it in the accusative conjoins it to النَّفس, and قصاص is its khabar, on the basis that it is written in the Torah. Whoever reads it in the nominative conjoins it to the position of أنّ and what it governs; so it is a mubtadaʾ, also written [in the Torah], and قصاص is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. It has also been said that it is a mubtadaʾ cut off from what precedes it, on the basis that it is not written [in the Torah]. This is cut off only according to the reading of whoever makes الْعين and what follows it accusative and makes الجروح nominative; as for whoever makes الْعين and what follows it nominative and makes الجروح nominative, it is all conjoined, part of it to part; and that is the reading of al-Kisāʾī.

mekki-muskil:46-46.t:
His saying {مُصدقا}: the first is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The second مُصدقا, if you wish, you conjoin to the first, also as a ḥāl from عِيسَى, as emphasis; or, if you wish, you make it a ḥāl from الْإِنْجِيل. الْإِنْجِيل is of the pattern إفعيل, derived from النجل ("origin"), as though it is the root of religion to which one returns and which one follows. التوراة is derived from وري الزند (the striking of the fire-stick), which is the light that comes out of its fire, so it is as though it is a light by which one is illuminated in religion. القرآن is derived from قريت المَاء فِي الْحَوْض ("I gathered the water in the basin"), when you collected it; so it is as though there have been gathered in it the rulings, the admonitions, the manners, the stories and the obligations, and all the benefits guiding to the paths of right guidance have been completed in it. Therefore Allah the Exalted said الْيَوْم أكملت لكم دينكُمْ, the verse.
His saying {وَهدى وموعظة}: accusative, conjoined to مُصدق. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read موعظة in the nominative, and [this] shows that this is in the position of the nominative; the nominative in that is by conjunction to His saying فِيهِ هدى وَنور.
His saying {مُصدقا} and مهيمنا: two ḥāls from الْكتاب.

mekki-muskil:49-49.t:
His saying {وَأَن احكم}: أَن is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to الْكتاب.
His saying {واحذرهم أَن يفتنوك}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ and mīm in واحذرهم, and it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl); or, if you wish, you make it a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {فَعَسَى الله أَن يَأْتِي}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by عسى. If you put it first and said فَعَسَى أَن يَأْتِي الله, it would be in the position of the nominative by عسى and would stand in place of the khabar (predicate) of عسى.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t:
His saying {وَيَقُول الَّذين آمنُوا}: whoever reads it in the accusative conjoins it according to the meaning, as though he assumed أَن يَأْتِي to be placed first, after عسى, and conjoined to it — since the meaning of فَعَسَى أَن يَأْتِي الله and وَعَسَى الله أَن يَأْتِي is one — so he conjoined according to the meaning. «[Translator's note: the source reads «قدر قديم», evidently for «قدّر تقديم» ("assumed the fronting of").]» Had he conjoined according to the wording, to أَن يَأْتِي while it is postponed after the name of Allah, it would not be permitted, just as it is far-fetched to say عَسى زيد أَن يقوم وَيَأْتِي عَمْرو, since عَسى زيد أَن يَأْتِي عَمْرو is not permitted. But when you put أَن first after عسى, it is good, as you say عَسى أَن يقوم زيد وَيَأْتِي عَمْرو; it is good just as عَسى أَن يقوم زيد وَيَأْتِي عَمْرو is good. If there were in the second clause something referring back to the first, all of this would be permitted, as in عَسى أَن يقوم زيد وَيَأْتِي أَبوهُ and عَسى زيد أَن يقوم وَيَأْتِي أَبوهُ; all of this is good and permitted, unlike the first, because if you said عَسى زيد أَن يقوم أَبوهُ it would be good. All of this is in the status of لَيْسَ زيد بِخَارِج وَلَا قَائِم عَمْرو, which is not permitted; but if أَبوهُ were in the place of عَمْرو, it would be permitted. That is its analogy, so make the analogy accordingly. It has also been said that وَيَقُول is conjoined to الْفَتْح, because it is in the sense of أَن يفتح; so it is conjoined to a noun, and an implied أَن was needed so that together with يَقُول it would be a maṣdar (verbal noun), and a noun would be conjoined to a noun. So it becomes in the status of the poet's saying:
... للبس عباءة وتقر عَيْني ... أحب إِلَيّ من لبس الشفوف ...
(Wearing a woollen cloak with my eye content is dearer to me than wearing sheer fabrics.)
The nominative in وَيَقُول is by qaṭʿ (detachment, i.e. a new start).
His saying {جهد أَيْمَانهم}: accusative as a maṣdar. إن in إِنَّهُم has kasra on the implied قَالُوا: "[they said:] indeed they…", because of the lām in its khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His saying {يُحِبهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ}: a naʿt (adjective) of قوم; likewise أَذِلَّة and أعزة. يجاهدون is also a naʿt of them, and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from them. The reference by the people described in this place is to the Rightly-Guided Caliphs after the Prophet, Allah bless him and grant him peace, and to those who followed them; and this is among what points to the establishment of their caliphate, may Allah be pleased with them all.

mekki-muskil:55-55.t: His saying {وهم رَاكِعُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in يُؤْتونَ, i.e. they give what purifies them before Allah while in the state of their bowing, i.e. while they are in their prayer; so the wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl, and on this meaning the verse was revealed concerning ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him. The clause may also have no position, being only a clause conjoined to the relative noun, the wāw not being the wāw of the ḥāl, and the verse is general.

mekki-muskil:57-57.t: His saying {وَالْكفَّار}: whoever reads it in the genitive conjoins it to الَّذين in His saying من الَّذين أُوتُوا; so they are described with play and mockery just as those who were given the Book were described with it, because of His saying إِنَّا كَفَيْنَاك الْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ, by which He means the disbelievers of Quraysh. Whoever reads it in the accusative conjoins it to الَّذين in His saying لَا تَتَّخِذُوا الَّذين, and they are excluded from the description of mockery and play.

mekki-muskil:59-59.t:
His saying {إِلَّا أَن آمنا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by تنقمون.
His saying {وَأَن أَكْثَرَكُم}: conjoined to it.

mekki-muskil:60-60.t: His saying {وَعبد الطاغوت}: whoever reads the bāʾ with fatḥa (وَعَبَدَ) makes it a past verb and makes الطاغوت accusative by it. In عبد is the pronoun of من in His saying من لَعنه الله; no plural pronoun appears in عبد, by construing it according to the wording of من, though its meaning is plural; therefore He said مِنْهُم, and had it been construed according to the meaning He would have said عبدُوا. من in His saying من لَعنه الله is in the position of the nominative on the omission of a muḍāf; its implied form is "the curse of whoever Allah has cursed" (لعن من لَعنه الله), i.e. "it is the curse of…"; so the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the muḍāf are both omitted. It has also been said that من is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) for بشر, a badal of a thing for a thing, being the same as it. مثوبة is accusative as tafsīr (specification). Whoever reads the bāʾ of عبد with ḍamma (عَبُد) makes it a noun on the pattern فَعُل, built for intensiveness in the worship of the ṭāghūt, like their saying رجل فطن and يقظ for one in whom acuity and alertness abound; so the meaning is "and He made of them those who went to extremes in the worship of the ṭāghūt." The origin of this pattern is for adjectives, and عبد is originally an adjective, but it was used here in the way nouns are used while keeping, in the pattern of adjectives, to its origin, just as they used الأبرق and الأبطح in the way nouns are used, so they were broken-pluralized as nouns are — one says الأباطح and الأبارق — yet they were not declined, like أحمر, their origin being the adjective.

mekki-muskil:61-61.t: His saying {وَقد دخلُوا بالْكفْر} وهم قد خَرجُوا بِهِ: His saying بالْكفْر is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise بِهِ. The meaning is: they entered as disbelievers and went out as disbelievers. He did not inform about them that they entered carrying something; He only informed about them that they entered holding disbelief as their belief.

mekki-muskil:68-68.t: His saying {مَا أنزل}: ما is in the position of the nominative by its verb, which is وليزيدن. كلما is an adverbial, and what governs it is أوقدوا; it contains the meaning of condition, so it must have an apodosis, and its apodosis is أطفأها.

mekki-muskil:69-69.t: His saying {والصابئون}: nominative by conjunction to the position of إنّ and what it governs. The khabar (predicate) of إنّ is intended before الصابئين, and therefore conjunction to the position was permitted; the khabar is من آمن, intended as fronted, so the proper place of والصابئون and النصارى is after يَحْزَنُونَ. This assumption was needed only because conjunction to the position in [the case of] إنّ is not permitted except after the statement is complete and the noun of إنّ and its khabar have ended, so that one conjoins to the position of the clause. Al-Farrāʾ said it is conjoined to the latent pronoun in هادوا; that is a mistake, because it requires that the Sabians and the Christians be Jews. Moreover, conjoining to a nominative pronoun before it is emphasized, or before something standing in the place of emphasis separates them, is ugly according to some grammarians. It has been said: الصابئون is nominative according to its original state before إنّ entered the clause. It has been said: الصابئون is nominative only because إنّ shows no overt effect on الَّذين, so the conjoined noun remained nominative according to its original state before إنّ entered the clause. It has been said: it is nominative only because it came according to the dialect of Balḥārith, who say رَأَيْت الزيدان with alif. It has been said: إنّ is in the sense of نعم ("yes"). And it has been said: the khabar of إنّ is omitted and implied, and the second points to it; so the conjunction with الصابئين came only after the statement was complete and the noun of إنّ and its khabar had ended; al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad held this. The school of Sībawayh is that the khabar of the second is what is omitted, and the khabar of إنّ is the one at the end of the statement, intended as fronted before الصابئين; so the conjunction to the position comes, in meaning, after the khabar of إنّ.

mekki-muskil:71-71.t:
His saying {وَحَسبُوا أَلا تكون فتْنَة}: whoever reads تكون in the nominative makes أَن the one lightened from the heavy (أنّ), implies the hāʾ with it, and تكون is the khabar (predicate) of أنّ; he makes حسبوا in the sense of "they were certain," because أنّ is for emphasis, and emphasis is permitted only with certainty, so it is its counterpart and equivalent. أَن is in the position of the accusative by حسب and stands in place of the two objects of حسب; its implied form is أَنه لَا تكون فتْنَة ("that there will be no trial"). On this assumption, أَن ought properly to be written separate, because the implied hāʾ comes between أَن and the lām of لا in meaning and in assumption, so its joining to the lām is barred. Whoever reads تكون in the accusative makes أَن the one that puts the verb in the accusative, and makes حسب in the sense of doubt, since no emphasis follows it, because the light أَن is not for emphasis; it is only for a thing that may or may not happen, so doubt is its counterpart and equivalent. The doubled one (أنّ) enters only to emphasize a thing that has happened and become established; therefore حسب with the doubled أنّ is for certainty and with the light one for doubt. If before أَن there were a verb not suitable for doubt, it could only be lightened from the heavy, and it would not be permitted to make the verb accusative by it, as in His saying, exalted is He, أَن لَا يرجع إِلَيْهِم and علم أَن سَيكون; لا and the sīn are a compensation for the omission of the doubling of أنّ. If before أَن there occurred a verb suitable only for what is not affirmation, nothing but the accusative would be permitted in the verb, as in your saying طمعت أَن تقوم ("I hoped that you would stand"), أشفق أَن تقوم ("I fear that you will stand"), and أخشى أَن تقوم ("I am afraid that you will stand"); in these only the accusative after أَن is permitted, and أَن with it cannot be lightened from the heavy. So these are three categories: a verb in the sense of firmness and certainty, with which there can only be the nominative after أَن, and أَن can only be lightened from the heavy; a verb in the opposite sense of firmness and certainty, with which there can only be the accusative after أَن, and أَن with it can only be other than lightened from the heavy; and a third verb that admits both, so both are permitted with it. These principles are the preferred choice among the people of knowledge, and other than what we have mentioned may be permitted by way of figurative usage and latitude.
His saying {فعموا وصموا}: the pronoun is plural only in reference back to those mentioned, and كثير is a badal (substitute) for the pronoun. It has been said: كثير is nominative on an implied mubtadaʾ (subject) indicated by عموا وصموا, its implied form being "the blindness and deafness are many of them" (الْعَمى والصم كثير مِنْهُم); and it has been said that the implied form is "the blind and the deaf among them are many" (الْعمي والصم مِنْهُم كثير). It has been said: the pronoun is plural while preceding [its noun], according to the dialect of those who say أكلوني البراغيث ("the fleas ate me"), and كثير is nominative by what precedes it. If you made كثيرا accusative in speech, it would be permitted, making it a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "much blindness and deafness" (عمى وصمما كثيرا).

mekki-muskil:73-73.t:
His saying {ثَالِث ثَلَاثَة}: it is not permitted to give ثَالِث tanwīn, because it is in the sense of "one of three," so there is no verbal meaning in it. It is not in the status of هَذَا ثَالِث اثْنَيْنِ ("this one makes two into three"), because that has a verbal meaning, since its meaning is "he makes two into three by himself"; so tanwīn is permitted in it.
His saying {وَمَا من إِلَه إِلَّا إِلَه وَاحِد}: إِلَه is a badal (substitute) for the position of من إِلَه, because من is redundant (zāʾida); so it is nominative. In speech the accusative إِلَّا إِلَهًا وَاحِدًا is permitted, as an exception. Al-Kisāʾī permitted the genitive as a badal for the wording of من إِلَه; that is far-fetched, because من is not added in an affirmative statement.

mekki-muskil:79-79.t: His saying {لبئس مَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ}: ما is an indefinite noun in the position of the accusative, i.e. "how evil a thing it was that they used to do" (لبئس شَيْئا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَهُ); so what comes after ما is an adjective of it. It has also been said that ما is in the sense of الَّذِي, in the position of the nominative by بئس, i.e. "evil indeed is the thing that they used to do" (لبئس الشَّيْء الَّذِي كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَهُ). The hāʾ is omitted from the adjective [clause] and from the ṣila (relative clause).

mekki-muskil:80-80.t: His saying {لبئس مَا قدمت لَهُم أنفسهم أَن سخط الله}: أَن is in the position of the nominative on an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); its implied form is "it is that Allah was angry" (هُوَ أَن سخط الله). It has been said: in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for ما, on the basis that ما is indefinite. And it has been said: on the omission of the lām, i.e. "because Allah was angry" (لِأَن سخط الله).

mekki-muskil:82-82.t: His saying {عَدَاوَة}: accusative as tafsīr (specification), and like it is مَوَدَّة.

mekki-muskil:83-83.t: His saying {تفيض}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أَعينهم, because ترى is from seeing with the eye.

mekki-muskil:84-84.t: His saying {لَا نؤمن}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from those speaking of themselves in لنا, as you say مَالك قَائِما ("why are you standing?").

mekki-muskil:85-85.t:
His saying {تجْرِي}: in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنات.
His saying {خَالِدين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in فأثابهم.

mekki-muskil:89-89.t: His saying {فَصِيَام ثَلَاثَة أَيَّام}: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is a fast of three days" (فَعَلَيهِ صِيَام ثَلَاثَة أَيَّام).

mekki-muskil:94-94.t: His saying {بِشَيْء من الصَّيْد}: من is partitive, because what is forbidden is specifically the game of the land, and because the prohibition applies specifically in the state of iḥrām. It has also been said that من is for specifying the genus: when He said ليبلونكم الله بِشَيْء, it was not known of what genus it was, so He made it clear and said من الصَّيْد, as you say لأعطينك شَيْئا من الذَّهَب ("I will surely give you something of gold").

mekki-muskil:95-95.t:
His saying {وَأَنْتُم حرم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in تقتلُوا; and متعمدا is a ḥāl from the nominative latent pronoun in قَتله.
His saying {فجزاء مثل مَا قتل من النعم}: جَزَاء is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is a compensation" (فَعَلَيهِ جَزَاء). Whoever gives جَزَاء tanwīn makes مثل an adjective of it, and من النعم another adjective of جَزَاء; it is also possible for مثل to be a badal (substitute) for جَزَاء. من in the status of من النعم is not attached to جَزَاء, because it would then fall within its ṣila (complement), and the adjective does not enter the ṣila of the one described, since it comes only after the one described is complete with its ṣila. If you made من attached to جَزَاء, it would enter its ṣila, while you have already put مثل before it, which is a badal or an adjective; and the badal and the adjective come only after the relative [element] is complete with its ṣila; so that would lead to separating the ṣila from the relative [element] by the badal or the naʿt (adjective). This is not in the status of جَزَاء سَيِّئَة بِمِثْلِهَا, in which the bāʾ may be attached to جَزَاء, because it is neither described nor has a badal; it is only in genitive construct, and the muḍāf ilayhi is included in the ṣila and part of the completion of the muḍāf; and all of it being included in the ṣila, that is good and permitted. مثل in this reading is in the sense of "equivalent" (مماثل), and the implied form is "then a compensation equivalent to what he killed" — meaning in value or in physical form, according to the disagreement of the scholars about that. If you took مثل according to its wording, the meaning would become "then upon him is the compensation of the like of what was killed of the game," whereas what is due from him is only the compensation of the killed animal itself, not the compensation of its like; because if he paid the compensation of the like of what was killed of the game, he would be paying only the compensation of what he did not kill, since he did not kill the like of the killed animal. So it is sound that the meaning is: "then upon him is a compensation equivalent to the killed animal, judged by two just men." Therefore the reading with the genitive construct (فجزاءُ مثلِ) was considered far-fetched by a group, because it requires that the killer owe the compensation of the like of the game he killed. It was permitted according to them only in the sense of the Arabs' saying أَنِّي لأكرم مثلك ("I surely honour the like of you"), by which they mean "I honour you." On this basis He put الجزاء in genitive construct with مثل of the killed animal, meaning the killed animal itself; so it is as though the implied form is "then upon him is the compensation of what was killed of the game." On this basis the scholars interpreted the saying of Allah the Exalted كمن مثله فِي الظُّلُمَات: its meaning is "like one who is in darkness"; had it been taken according to the apparent sense, it would be the like of the disbeliever that is in darkness. المثل and المثل are one. من النعم, in the reading of whoever puts الجزاء in genitive construct with مثل, is an adjective of جَزَاء; and it is good for من to be attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun), so that it is not an adjective of it, but rather the maṣdar is made transitive to من النعم. If you make it an adjective, من is attached to the omitted khabar, namely فَعَلَيهِ; and if you do not make it an adjective, it is attached to جَزَاء, as it is attached in His saying جَزَاء سَيِّئَة بِمِثْلِهَا, because الجزاء has been neither described nor given a badal, so there is no separation between the ṣila and the relative [element]. But when you give جَزَاء tanwīn, attaching من to جَزَاء is not good, for the reasons we have given.
His saying {هَديا}: it is accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in بِهِ; it may also be accusative as bayān (clarification) or as a maṣdar. بَالغ is a naʿt of هدي, and tanwīn is implied in it; therefore it occurs as a naʿt of an indefinite noun.
His saying {أَو كَفَّارَة}: conjoined to جَزَاء, i.e. "or upon him is an expiation." Whoever gives كَفَّارَة tanwīn makes الطَّعَام nominative as a badal for كَفَّارَة. صياما is accusative as bayān (clarification).

mekki-muskil:96-96.t: His saying {مَتَاعا}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because His saying أحل لكم is in the sense of "I have given you enjoyment of it" (أمتعتكم بِهِ إمتاعا), in the status of كتاب الله عَلَيْكُم. حرما is the khabar (predicate) of دَامَ.

mekki-muskil:97-97.t: His saying {ذَلِك لِتَعْلَمُوا}: ذا is in the position of the nominative with the meaning "the matter is that" (الْأَمر ذَلِك); it may also be in the position of the accusative with the meaning "Allah did that so that you may know" (فعل الله ذَلِك لِتَعْلَمُوا).

mekki-muskil:101-101.t:
His saying {لَا تسألوا عَن أَشْيَاء}: al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and al-Māzinī said: أَشْيَاء is originally شيئاء, on the pattern فعلاء. When its use became frequent, two hamzas with an alif between them were felt to be heavy, so the first hamza, which is the lām of the root, was moved before the fāʾ of the root, which is the shīn, and it became أَشْيَاء on the pattern لفعاء. Because its origin is فعلاء, like حمراء, it is a diptote. According to them it is a collective noun (ism li-l-jamʿ), not a plural of شَيْء. Al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayd said: it is a diptote because it resembles حَمْرَاء, since the Arabs say in the plural أشياوات just as they say حمراوات. They are obliged [by this] not to decline اسْم and ابْن, because of the Arabs' saying in the plural سماوات and ابناوات. Al-Akhfash, al-Farrāʾ and al-Ziyādī said: أَشْيَاء is of the pattern أفعلاء, originally أشيئاء, like هين and أهوناء; it is a diptote because of the feminine hamza, but it was lightened: the first hamza, which is the lām of the root, was replaced with yāʾ because of the kasra before it, then it was dropped for lightness because of frequent use. So شَيْء according to them is originally شييء on the pattern فيعل, like هين, which is originally هيّن on فيعل, and was before assimilation هيون on فيعل, like ميت, then lightened; except that the ʿayn of the root in شَيْء is yāʾ and the ʿayn of the root in هين is wāw, because it is from هان يهون, like ميت. This plural has no parallel, because أفعلاء does not occur as a plural of فيعل such that this would be its parallel; هين and أهوناء is anomalous and is not to be taken as a basis for analogy. Moreover, its omission and weakening ran contrary to analogy; so this view departs, in its plural and its weakening, from both analogy and attested usage. Moreover, they are obliged to form the diminutive of أَشْيَاء as شويات or شييئات, and no one has said that; its diminutive is only أَشْيَاء. «[Translator's note: the diminutive form is written in the source with the same letters as أَشْيَاء; the vowelled diminutive أُشَيَّاء is evidently meant.]» That is required of them in the diminutive only because every plural that is not one of the patterns of the paucal plural is treated in the diminutive by being returned to its singular; then the singular is made diminutive, and then it is pluralized in diminutive form with alif and tāʾ, or with wāw and nūn if it denotes rational beings. أفعلاء is not one of the patterns of the paucal plural. The patterns of the plural of paucity are four: أَفعَال, أفعلة, أفعل and فعلة; these are made diminutive on their own wording and are not returned to the singular. Al-Māzinī said: I asked al-Akhfash about the diminutive of أَشْيَاء, and he said: أشياء. Al-Māzinī said: so I said to him: according to your view that it is أفعلاء, it must be returned to the singular, made diminutive, and then pluralized. And al-Akhfash was silenced. Abū Ḥātim said: أَشْيَاء is أَفعَال, plural of شَيْء, like بيت and أبيات; it ought to be declined, except that it was heard undeclined. This view runs according to analogy in the plural, because the plural of فَعْل frequently occurs as أَفعَال; but it departs from analogy in its not being declined, for no undeclined أَفعَال occurs in the speech of the Arabs such that this would be its parallel. Some of the people of reasoning said: أَشْيَاء is originally أشيئاء on the pattern أفعلاء, as al-Akhfash said, except that its singular is فعيل, like صديق and أصدقاء; then it was weakened as previously described, by lightening the hamza and dropping the compensation «[Translator's note: the source has «فَاعل», evidently for «فأُعِلّ» ("then it was weakened").]». The omission in the plural is good because of its omission from the singular, and it was omitted from the singular only for lightness because of frequent use, since شَيْء applies to every named thing, whether accident, body or substance. It is a diptote because of the feminine hamza in the plural. This is a good view, running according to analogy in the plural and in the non-declension, were it not that the diminutive objects to it just as it objected to al-Akhfash.
His saying {إِن تبد لكم تَسُؤْكُمْ}: a condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of أَشْيَاء.

mekki-muskil:103-103.t: His saying {من بحيرة}: من is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and بحيرة is in the position of the accusative by جعل.

mekki-muskil:104-104.t: His saying {حَسبنَا مَا وجدنَا}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is مَا وجدنَا.

mekki-muskil:106-106.t:
His saying {إِذا حضر}: what governs إِذا is شَهَادَة; الْوَصِيَّة does not govern it, because the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern what precedes the muḍāf; moreover, الْوَصِيَّة is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so what it governs is not put before it. What governs حين الْوَصِيَّة is the causes of death, as He said حَتَّى إِذا جَاءَ أحدهم الْمَوْت قَالَ — and the saying does not come from him after death; rather, its meaning is "until, when the causes of death come to one of them, he says." It has been said that what governs حين is حضر; and it has been said that it is a badal (substitute) for إِذا, so that what governs حين is also الشهادة.
His saying {اثْنَان}: nominative as the khabar (predicate) of شَهَادَة on the omission of a muḍāf; its implied form is "the testimony of two" (شَهَادَة اثْنَيْنِ), because the testimony cannot be the two persons themselves, since bodies cannot be the khabar of a maṣdar; so a maṣdar was implied so as to be the khabar of a maṣdar. Likewise أَو آخرَانِ من غَيْركُمْ is conjoined to اثْنَان on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "or the testimony of two others" (أَو شَهَادَة آخَرين). «[Translator's note: the source says "an omitted muḍāf ilayhi" here, though its own implied form shows an omitted muḍāf.]» It has also been said that إِذا حضر is the khabar of شَهَادَة, and اثْنَان are nominative by their verb, which is شَهَادَة.
His saying {تحبسونهما من بعد الصَّلَاة}: an adjective of آخرَانِ, in the position of the nominative.
His saying {إِن أَنْتُم ضَرَبْتُمْ} up to His saying {الْمَوْت}: a parenthesis between the one described and its adjective. The apodosis of إِن, which is the condition, is dispensed with by the preceding speech, because the meaning of اثْنَان ذَوا عدل مِنْكُم أَو آخرَانِ من غَيْركُمْ is the meaning of a command to do that, while its wording is the wording of a statement. The apodosis of إِذا is also dispensed with by the preceding speech, namely His saying شَهَادَة بَيْنكُم, because its meaning is "you ought to bear witness when death approaches one of you." «[Translator's note: the source says «جَوَاب إِذا الَّتِي هِيَ الشَّرْط» in the first clause, where إِن is evidently meant, as the following «جَوَاب إِذا أَيْضا» shows; translated accordingly.]»
His saying {فيقسمان بِاللَّه}: the fāʾ is for conjoining a clause to a clause. It may also be the answer of a conditional, because تحبسونهما means a command to do that; so it is the answer to the command indicated by the speech, as though He said "when you detain them, they swear" (إِذا حبستموا أقسما), since the meaning of إِن ارتبتم is "if you doubt" the statement of the two others not from among you.
His saying {لَا نشتري}: the answer to His saying فيقسمان, because أقسم is answered with what an oath is answered with.
His saying {لَا نشتري بِهِ}: the hāʾ refers to the meaning, because the implied form is "we will not sell for a price the distortion of our testimony" (لَا نشتري بتحريف شهادتنا ثمنا); then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. It has also been said that the hāʾ refers to الشهادة, but it is masculine because it is a saying (قول), as He said فارزقوهم مِنْهُ, referring the hāʾ to what is divided (الْمقسم) because the word "division" (الْقِسْمَة) indicates it.
His saying {لَا نشتري بِهِ ثمنا}: its meaning is "something having a price" (ذَا ثمن), because the price is not bought; what is bought is only that which has a price, namely the priced item. It is like His saying, exalted is He, اشْتَروا بآيَات الله ثمنا, i.e. something having a price.
His saying {وَلَو كَانَ ذَا قربى}: in كَانَ is its noun (ism), i.e. "even if the one for whom testimony is given were a relative of the witness."
His saying {وَلَا نكتم شَهَادَة الله}: the testimony is put in genitive construct with Allah only because He is the one who commanded its delivery and forbade its concealment.
His saying {فآخران}: nominative by an implied verb or as a mubtadaʾ (subject); يقومَانِ is a naʿt (adjective) of them, and من الَّذين is its khabar.
